Protect Yourself

Start with the accounts that control password resets, the devices you use daily, and the files you need to recover.

  • Password managers and recovery

    Use a unique password for each account and keep recovery details safe.

  • Passkeys and multi-factor authentication

    Use stronger sign-in on accounts that support it.

  • Device and software updates

    Enable automatic updates and schedule restarts where needed.

  • Messaging and banking scams

    Verify the sender through a number or app you already trust.

  • Backups and ransomware

    Keep a separate copy of critical files and practise restoring one.

  • Downloads and app permissions

    Start with the official publisher or a trusted store.

  • Home networks and privacy

    Review device access, router updates, and which accounts can change settings.

Online privacy and app permissions

Security Toolkit

Have I Been Pwned

Individuals · Web

Check whether an email address appears in known breaches indexed by the service.

A negative result cannot rule out a breach. Search an address you are entitled to check.

Bitwarden

Individuals and teams · Desktop, mobile and browser

Store unique passwords and supported passkeys in a vault.

Plan account recovery and secure the vault before depending on it.

Microsoft Defender Antivirus

Windows users and administrators · Windows

Use the malware protection built into supported Windows installations.

Keep protection updates current. A clean scan alone does not close an investigation.

VirusTotal

IT support and analysts · Web

Compare scanner findings for a public file or URL, or look up an existing report.

Never upload confidential files, private URLs, tokens or customer data to public scanning services. Submissions can be shared.

Wireshark

IT support and network operators · Windows, macOS and Linux

Inspect authorised packet captures during network troubleshooting.

Captures may contain sensitive data. Limit collection to networks you are authorised to inspect.
